claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a dual-phase, fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The as-cast lamellar microstructure has relatively straight, continuous colony and phase boundaries.
Microcracks initiate at the internal colony or phase boundaries during room-temperature tensile deformation.
An 8–10% cold-rolling reduction followed by optimized annealing can produce serrated, wavy boundaries in the lamellar colonies.
Serrated boundaries create local geometric irregularities and a more heterogeneous stress distribution.
Serrated boundaries promote crack deflection and blunting.
A tortuous crack path increases the energy required for interfacial crack propagation.
The heterogeneous microstructure improves load transfer.
The heterogeneous microstructure enhances strain hardening.
Crack arrest, improved load transfer, and enhanced strain hardening suppress premature microcrack formation and coalescence.
Producing serrated boundaries will increase yield strength relative to the as-cast straight-boundary baseline.
Producing serrated boundaries will increase room-temperature tensile elongation relative to the as-cast straight-boundary baseline.
The treatment will delay crack initiation and slow crack propagation.
The cited AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy demonstrates that a lamellar eutectic HEA can combine high strength and high room-temperature tensile ductility.
The proposed strategy requires preservation of the dual-phase lamellar structure and avoidance of coarsening or phase instability.
The strategy is expected to apply to eutectic HEAs dominated by lamellar colonies rather than alloys with entirely different morphologies.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% statistically significant increase in both yield strength and tensile ductility is designated as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The baseline characterizes the conventionally cast lamellar alloy as undergoing rapid microcracking and brittle-type room-temperature failure, whereas the cited evidence characterizes as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 as having an unprecedented combination of high room-temperature tensile ductility and high fracture strength.
